one_liner: NotebookLM is Google's AI notebook/research assistant; the enterprise edition (NotebookLM Enterprise, part of Gemini Enterprise) lets organizations create grounded notebooks from their own documents with programmatic notebook management.
self_serve_evidence: Access requires purchasing a Gemini Notebook Enterprise license and setting up a Google Cloud project/Cloud Identity; the API is in preview and tied to the Discovery Engine service rather than open self-signup.
api_surface: REST API (Discovery Engine-based) supporting notebooks.create/get/listRecentlyViewed/batchDelete/share plus a podcast-generation method; narrow CRUD+sharing surface, no query/chat endpoint documented.
existing_mcp_detail: No official MCP found for NotebookLM or NotebookLM Enterprise. Several unofficial community MCP servers exist for the consumer notebooklm.google.com product, typically via browser automation rather than a real API.
blocker: Requires a paid Google Cloud/Gemini Enterprise license plus project setup; API is preview-stage with a very limited surface (notebook CRUD/sharing only, no ask/query endpoint).
notes: Consumer NotebookLM (notebooklm.google.com) has no public API at all. Only the paid Enterprise edition (via Gemini Enterprise/Discovery Engine) exposes a preview REST API, and even that covers notebook management, not the core 'ask questions of sources' capability.

one_liner: Otter.ai is an AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes, and summarizes conversations and meetings in real time.
self_serve_evidence: The official MCP server is self-serve OAuth for platforms like Claude/ChatGPT/Cursor, but Otter's own help center states 'we currently do not have a public API key at this time' and routes custom/enterprise integration requests to sales.
api_surface: No general-purpose public REST API; access is exclusively through the official OAuth-authenticated MCP server, which exposes meeting/transcript retrieval and search-style tools rather than a full CRUD API.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Otter MCP Server at https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp, documented at help.otter.ai, OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions.
blocker: No traditional API-key/REST access exists for building custom integrations beyond the MCP server; broader API access requires contacting Otter support/sales.
notes: Unofficial community projects also exist and appear to reverse-engineer Otter's internal endpoints, underscoring that there's no sanctioned public API key.

one_liner: Fathom is an AI note-taker that automatically records, transcribes, and summarizes video meetings (Zoom, Google Meet, Teams).
self_serve_evidence: Official docs state 'anyone can browse the API docs and start building' and describe generating an API key and making the first call 'in minutes' with no approval step.
api_surface: REST API (developers.fathom.ai) covering meeting summaries, transcripts, and action items, plus webhooks and official TypeScript/Python SDKs; OAuth apps supported for customer-facing integrations; rate-limited to 60 calls/minute per user.
existing_mcp_detail: Unofficial community MCP server exists on GitHub. No Fathom-operated official MCP server was found in the docs.
notes: API keys are user-scoped and only access meetings recorded by that user or shared to their team; exact plan requirements for API access were not explicitly stated in the docs reviewed.

one_liner: Consensus (consensus.app) is an AI-powered search engine that finds and synthesizes insights from over 200 million peer-reviewed academic research papers.
self_serve_evidence: Official docs state 'No account is needed to get started, connect directly and try it out' for the MCP server, with OAuth2 for Claude/ChatGPT/Cursor/Codex and Bearer-token API keys for enterprise use.
api_surface: Primarily exposed via MCP: a Search tool over 200M+ papers (filterable by study type, year, journal quality/SJR, sample size, duration) and a Fetch tool for full paper details (currently ChatGPT-exclusive); no broad standalone public REST API surface documented.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Consensus MCP server documented at docs.consensus.app/docs/mcp; supports Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code (Copilot), Windsurf, and Codex.
notes: Deeper functionality tiers are gated by the user's Consensus subscription plan rather than by the API access itself. The 'OAuth requested' status mentioned in the task appears resolved in current docs — OAuth2 is live for major AI platforms.

one_liner: Reducto is an agentic document platform/API that parses messy PDFs, tables, forms, and scanned documents into structured, LLM-ready data.
self_serve_evidence: Users create a free account at studio.reducto.ai and self-generate an API key immediately (REDUCTO_API_KEY), with no sales approval step documented in the quickstart.
api_surface: REST API with Parse, Extract (schema-based), Split, Edit, and async job endpoints, plus job management; official Python/Node/Go SDKs and an official MCP server exposing 11 tools.
existing_mcp_detail: Official 'mcp-server-reducto', documented at docs.reducto.ai/mcp-server; supports OAuth device-code login, REDUCTO_API_KEY env var, or shared CLI credentials.
notes: Free-trial self-serve tier exists alongside enterprise/batch pricing, but this doesn't block basic API access.

one_liner: Devin (by Cognition) is an autonomous AI software engineer that plans, writes, tests, and ships code changes in its own sandboxed environment.
self_serve_evidence: Users generate an API key from account settings and use it directly with both the REST API and MCP server; no manual approval step is documented.
api_surface: REST API (v3, e.g., GET /v3/self for org info) for session and org management, plus an official MCP server exposing repository-wiki/docs search, session management, playbook management, knowledge management, scheduling, and integration management tools.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Devin MCP server at https://mcp.devin.ai/, documented at docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-mcp; uses the same API-key auth as the REST API.
notes: Legacy API keys are explicitly not supported; org-scoped service-user keys, enterprise service-user keys, or personal access tokens are required.

one_liner: Higgsfield is an AI image and video generation platform offering 30+ creative models, accessible via a web app, CLI, and MCP server for agent-driven content generation.
self_serve_evidence: The CLI/MCP is installed via npm (@higgsfield/cli) and authenticated through a browser-based 'higgsfield auth login' flow tied to a user's Higgsfield account, with no manual approval step described.
api_surface: CLI + official MCP server + a Python SDK for generation workflows: text/image-to-image (30+ models, up to 4K) and text/image-to-video (up to 15s, multiple model families), plus character training and generation-history browsing. This is a narrow, generation-focused surface rather than a broad general-purpose REST API.
existing_mcp_detail: Higgsfield's own help center describes adding 'the Higgsfield MCP server URL' to an agent's settings and authenticating via the Higgsfield account, integrating with Claude, Cursor, and other MCP clients.
blocker: Documentation is thin and scattered across a help-center article, GitHub repos, and a marketing CLI page rather than a unified API reference; the account-login-based auth model may complicate fully headless/server-side automation, and rate limits/pricing for programmatic use were not confirmed.
notes: This is a genuinely obscure product with limited authoritative documentation. Could not verify a formal REST API reference, pricing, or rate limits with confidence — treat this entry as directional rather than fully confirmed.

one_liner: Mermaid CLI (mmdc) is an open-source command-line tool that renders Mermaid diagram-as-code definitions into SVG, PNG, or PDF files.
self_serve_evidence: It is an MIT-licensed npm package (@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli) that anyone can install and run locally (or via Docker/npx) with no account, key, or approval required — because it is not a hosted service at all.
api_surface: Not a network API: mmdc takes a .mmd file as input and outputs SVG/PNG/PDF locally; there's also a Node.js library API for programmatic in-process use. No REST/GraphQL surface exists for the CLI project itself.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple unofficial community MCP wrappers shell out to mermaid-cli. Note: the separate commercial product 'Mermaid Chart' (mermaid.ai) has its own official hosted MCP server, but that is a distinct SaaS product from the open-source mermaid-cli.
blocker: none — but note this is fundamentally a local tool, not a hosted vendor API; 'buildability' here means wrapping the CLI as a tool server rather than integrating against a multi-tenant API with auth/rate limits.
notes: Confirmed via the official repo README: mermaid-cli is purely a local/offline rendering tool (npm package + Docker image), with no hosted SaaS or API variant. If the research intent was the hosted 'Mermaid Chart' commercial product instead, that one does have an official API/MCP and a different buildability profile.

one_liner: Retrieval of YouTube video transcripts/captions programmatically — via Google's official (ownership-restricted) YouTube Data API v3 Captions endpoint, or via third-party wrapper services like transcriptapi.com that scrape public caption data for arbitrary videos.
self_serve_evidence: Google's official captions.download requires OAuth2 and only works for videos the authenticated user/channel owns or has edit rights to (otherwise a 403 'permissions not sufficient' error), so it is not usable for fetching transcripts of arbitrary third-party videos; unofficial wrapper services offer self-serve API-key access to transcripts for any public video instead.
api_surface: Official: YouTube Data API v3 captions.list/captions.download methods — narrow and ownership-gated, with optional machine-translation via the tlang parameter. Unofficial: REST wrapper APIs that scrape YouTube's public timedtext/caption tracks to return transcripts for any public video, without OAuth.
existing_mcp_detail: Numerous unofficial YouTube-transcript MCP servers exist in the community ecosystem; none are officially operated by Google/YouTube.
blocker: The only official Google-sanctioned method cannot retrieve transcripts for videos the caller doesn't own/control, so a general-purpose 'get transcript for any YouTube video' agent tool must rely on unofficial/third-party scraping services, which carry YouTube ToS and reliability/breakage risk.
notes: transcriptapi.com is an unofficial third-party service unaffiliated with YouTube/Google; its availability, pricing, and ToS-compliance should be treated as a separate risk factor from the official Data API path.

one_liner: Grain is an AI meeting recorder/notetaker that captures, transcribes, and shares highlights from sales and team calls, with CRM/deal-intelligence add-ons.
self_serve_evidence: Personal Access Tokens (per-user) and Workspace Access Tokens (org-wide) are self-generated instantly from account settings, but building a public OAuth2 integration requires manually registering to obtain a client_id/client_secret.
api_surface: REST API (api.grain.com) covering recordings (list/retrieve/update/upload/download/transcripts), sharing/access control, tagging, users/teams/meeting-type enumeration, and webhooks; versioned via a Public-Api-Version header; rate-limited to 300 requests/minute. Plus an official MCP server with meeting-intelligence and contact-search tools, and Business/Enterprise-tier deal-intelligence/sales-coaching tools.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Grain MCP Server at https://api.grain.com/_/mcp, OAuth-authenticated, documented at developers.grain.com/mcp.
notes: Some MCP capabilities (Deal Intelligence, Sales Coaching) are gated to Business/Enterprise plans; core meeting/transcript access via PAT/WAT/REST is broadly self-serve.
